subject: Short-term throughput increase for holiday promo (BrightCart)
messages:
From: Miriam Santos <miriam.santos@brightcart.com>
To: jonas.weber@redwood.com
Cc: cto@brightcart.com
Date: 2025-10-10 09:12 -0400
Subject: Request: short-term throughput increase for holiday promo

Hi Jonas,

Quick note from BrightCart — we have an aggressive promotional window the week of Nov 28 that could push our inference traffic ~3x baseline for a 48-hour peak (mostly 12pm-2am UTC). We need a short-term plan to avoid throttling and maintain latency SLAs for checkout personalization.

Questions:
- Can Redwood support a 2.5–4x temporary throughput uplift for a 48–72 hour window?
- What are the commercial options (uplift fee vs PAYG overage rates vs pre-paid burst blocks)?
- If we exceed an agreed cap, how does true-up work and what are typical surcharges/credits?

I'm looping in our CTO (cc) and procurement will need rough pricing so we can decide quickly. We can share estimated QPS and tokens per request tomorrow — rough numbers now are: baseline 120 QPS, expected peak 360 QPS, mean tokens/request ~450.

Attachments: BrightCart_traffic_plan.xlsx (traffic projection, stub)

Thanks — Miriam
Miriam Santos
Head of Platform
BrightCart
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Miriam Santos <miriam.santos@brightcart.com>
Cc: cto@brightcart.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-10 11:03 -04:00
Subject: Re: Request: short-term throughput increase for holiday promo

Hi Miriam — thanks for the heads up and the projection file. We can support the uplift; below are three pragmatic commercial options depending on how BrightCart wants to balance predictability vs cost: 

1) Short-Term Reserved Headroom (recommended)
   - Reserve an ephemeral capacity block for the 48–72 hour window (2.5x or 4x).
   - One-time uplift fee (covers GPU reservation & priority routing) + usage at standard token rates.
   - If actual peak < reserved, we prorate the uplift fee to actual usage (no waste).

2) On-Demand Overrun (fast to enable)
   - Keep existing quotas; allow automatic overrun at a predefined surcharge (e.g., 1.6x standard token rate) with true-up post-window.
   - No upfront fee but less predictable invoice.

3) Prepaid Burst Credits
   - Purchase N hours of burst capacity upfront at a discounted rate (applied first during the window).
   - Good if you want budget certainty without a long-term commit.

Operational notes: we can set an automatic fallback to a compatible smaller model if capacity throttling would otherwise occur, and we can enable prefix/KV caching for checkout flows to reduce tokens.

Commercial levers we need from you: exact start/end times, expected sustained QPS during peak hours, and whether BrightCart is comfortable pre-authorizing an uplift invoice or prefers PAYG.

I've attached a short uplift_pricing_proposal.pdf stub showing sample math for 2.5x vs 4x. If you'd like, we can do a 30-minute call with our SRE/solutions engineer tomorrow to map the runbook.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Director, Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachment: uplift_pricing_proposal.pdf (pricing stub)
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, naomi.feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2025-10-10 12:15 -04:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightCart — short-term throughput increase / proposed commercial options

FYI forwarding BrightCart's ask. Key points:
- 48–72 hour window end of Nov (Black Friday week)
- Target: 3x peak (120 -> ~360 QPS), ~450 tokens/req
- Prefers minimal lead time; procurement will want a clear PO amount and quick DocuSign path

Proposed commercial approach (my suggestion):
- Offer a Short-Term Reserved Headroom at a 20% uplift fee discount if they sign a 3-month minimal commit (they get priority capacity, lower true-up exposure).
- Fallback: On-Demand Overrun at 1.5x token surcharge if they decline upfront fee.

If we give 20% off uplift fee, I want confirmation we can approve without further revenue sign-off (it's a one-off uplift fee — not affecting base ARR). Deal id: DC-8942.

Any objections? Also: would like to include an SLA credit (small, e.g., 5% invoice credit) only if we miss agreed p95 latency during the window.

We should also ensure SRE signs off on the fallback model plan and we'll instrument p95 latency metric specifically for the window.
